label: Bodleian Library MS. Elliott 254

metadata.label: Catalogue Description
metadata.value: Full catalogue record in Fihrist: Union Catalogue of Manuscripts from the Islamicate World

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Manuscript commissioned by the Mughal emperor Akbar (1542-1605), containing stories by the Persian poet Jami (1414-1492), entitled Baharistan (Garden of spring).

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Contents: MS. introduction by Sir Gore Ouseley entitled "Beharistan", dated Nov. 1817 (ff. iv-vii). Jami, Baharistan (ff. 1-67).

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Extent: 67 leaves. 300 x 195 mm (written area 170 x 83, frame-ruled).

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Layout: Written in 1 column of 14 lines.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Decoration: Illuminated frontispiece; 6 miniature paintings by the Mughal court artists; the margins decorated throughout with gold patterns and figures, some painted.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Binding: 19th-century red velvet over cardboard with brass centrepiece and corner pieces on upper and lower covers.

metadata.label: Provenance
metadata.value: Written for Akbar (1542-1605); from the collection of Sir Gore Ouseley (1770-1844); from the collection of John Bardoe Elliott; presented to Bodleian Library 1859.

metadata.label: Record Origin
metadata.value: Image descriptions based in part on Topsfield, A. (2007), Paintings from Mughal India.

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Illustration of: Jami, Baharistan. Abdullah Ibn Jafer presents the singing girl to the scholar who has been distracted from his studies and religion by his overpowering love for her.
